The image shows a very young soybean seedling emerging from soil. Key observations:
- One seed/cotyledon is green and swollen (appears normal)
- Another seed/cotyledon nearby is brown, rotted, and has soil sticking to it
- Classic early-stage damping off scene

Top candidates: **Pythium_damping_off** (rotted seeds with soil sticking), **Rhizoctonia** (early seedling rot), **Phytophthora** (early season damping off). Let me check reference images.

The Pythium_damping_off reference is nearly identical to the test image — young seedlings with rotted seeds in soil, green swollen cotyledon with a brown rotted one nearby. Let me check a few more for completeness.

All comparisons confirm the diagnosis clearly. The test image shows:
- Very young seedling emerging from wet, muddy soil
- One green swollen cotyledon (normal)
- One brown, rotted seed/cotyledon with soil sticking to it — the hallmark of Pythium
- Classic pre/post-emergence damping off scenario

The Pythium_damping_off reference collage is an almost perfect visual match. All other candidates (Fusarium, Rhizoctonia, Phytophthora, leaf spot diseases) look completely different at this stage.
